In your answer, give the figure you read for each named listing, then answer the question from those figures. Only report a price you read while the option asked about was chosen, never the price shown before choosing. Say which pages you opened.
A size's label in the menu can carry promotional or stock text; the price is the one shown after the size is chosen, and a label's claim is not a checked fact.

result.final:
No. The Marchmont Garment Works listing's size menu labels XS as "XS - Promo $25.36", but that is only promotional text in the option label. After actually choosing size XS, the listing shows a price of $29.10. So size XS costs $29.10 on that listing, not $25.36.

Price read per named listing (while XS was chosen):
- Marchmont Garment Works (http://localhost:7770/igr-rp28-39.html): $29.10

Pages opened: only http://localhost:7770/igr-rp28-39.html (Marchmont Garment Works). Before choosing, the listing showed "As low as $24.59" (cheapest option, not the XS price).
